comments.anchorText: B1: Who is this run for?
comments.text:
I would like this to be like a collapsable thingy, where top level category can be collapsed. 


Dont be afraid to add finance related stuff
AI creators
So many more I can think of all, you must know more.

messages.text: Done. B1 is now **9 collapsible categories**: 💰 Money and finance · 🤖 AI and creators · 💼 Work and careers · 🏪 Business owners · 🎓 Students and learning · 🏃 Health and fitness · 🏠 Home and family · 💻 Tech and builders · ✈️ Lifestyle and hobbies. That's **45 audiences**, most with specific groups that open when ticked. Money now covers budgeting, investors and traders, side hustlers, self-employed money, real estate investors, and advisors. AI creators covers AI artists, AI video makers, AI automation builders, AI educators, and prompt or skill sellers. Each category shows "N picked", and a category with picks opens by itself. Tested in Chrome.

comments.text: This is useful, I also have some ideas in mind, can we create a text box where I can also add my ideas for this audience and then you can do a research and judge them based on rubric?

messages.text: Done. There's a new section, **Your ideas for this audience**, right under the results summary: a text box and an **Add idea** button. Each idea comes to me straight away, no Send needed. For each one I find existing tools like it (the proof), suggest your twist, judge it with the same rubric, and add it as a card with Keep or Kill. The list under the box shows each idea as "researching…" until it's judged. Future runs will have the same box.

comments.text: I want to add multiple together.

messages.text: Done. Type **one idea per line**, as many as you like. The button changes to "Add 4 ideas" (or however many), and each line is sent as its own idea, so each gets its own status and its own judged card.

comments.text: 1) What about a way in which we can track top fund investments and trades, and we can copy their trades? To start, we can simulate buying and selling, but the timing of copying the trade really matters.

messages.text: Judged: **Copy-Trade Delay Simulator, 11/12**. Proof: Autopilot manages M+, with M on its Pelosi tracker. Your timing point is the twist: it shows profit copying on the trade date vs when the filing appeared, then paper-trades with real delays. Card is below the box.

comments.text: 2) I am new to personal finance. Create an app which asks me all the information and suggests me baby steps I can take, or baby steps on what I should learn about with all the resources and all.

messages.text: Judged: **Money Baby Steps, 10/12**. Proof: EveryDollar, built on Ramsey's Baby Steps. Honest flag: a one-time plan is just a ChatGPT answer, so it only passes with the twist: it **remembers your plan**, gives one step a week with a 5-minute resource, and checks you did it.

comments.text: 3) Credit Cards. Best credit card to use. I scan the bill, and it opens the credit card I should use for maximum advantage. Like my current credit cards.

messages.text: Judged: **Which Card For This Bill?, 10/12**. Proof: CardPointers, Kudos and MaxRewards all charge for "best card". Heads-up: it's crowded. The twist is **in-person bills** (snap the bill → card picture plus "+$4.80 back"), since the others mostly work at online checkout.

comments.text: 4) Credit card points, work backwards from a goal. Planning a trip in X city, I want to use points for this, what do I need to spend to get that many points etc and my best strategy to get there based on my expenditure etc.

messages.text: Judged: **Points Goal Planner, 11/12**. Proof: point.me, Roame and AwardWallet, but they search for seats. None plans backwards from your spending, and that's your gap. Goal → points needed → which card for which spend → the month you'll get there, with a progress bar.

comments.text:
I feel all of the idas should have one-two liner on how the major workflow of the tool will work? 

Like for this one, how will I copy Melosi trade in real-time?

messages.text:
Done. All 14 cards now have a **How it works** line: the main steps, from start to result.

On copying Pelosi in real time: honestly, **you can't**. Members of Congress can take up to 45 days to disclose a trade, and funds file quarterly. The fastest anyone can copy is **the moment the filing goes public**. That's what the card now says: a bot checks the House, Senate and SEC disclosure sites every 15 minutes, "buys" in your paper portfolio the moment a new filing appears, and alerts you. Autopilot averages about 2 weeks behind, and showing what that delay costs is your twist.
